comment: NFC policy for the S10+ (beyond2lte). Read by tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-nfc-diag.sh. The controller is a Samsung sec-nfc (S3FWRN5-family) part at I2C address 0x27 with an embedded secure element. Controller presence, firmware and the userspace stack are ENUMERATED per stage and the FIRST failing stage is reported. Configuration alone is NEVER a working NFC: the terminal verdict is NEEDS_OWNER_TEST until a physical tag is read. If the vendor kernel ships no usable controller driver, the honest verdict is BLOCKED_KERNEL / NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_DEVICE.

device.controller: Samsung sec-nfc (S3FWRN5-family) @ I2C 0x27 + embedded secure element
device.transport: Samsung sec_nfc misc character device /dev/sec-nfc (raw I2C; NOT a generic NCI adapter)

firmware_expected.provenance: owner SM-G975F vendor partition; not redistributable

verdicts.READY_FOR_TAG: controller enumerated, firmware present, NFC subsystem and a userspace client/daemon available — an owner may tap a tag (still NEEDS_OWNER_TEST)
verdicts.BLOCKED_KERNEL: no NFC controller node and no NFC driver module bound — the vendor kernel did not bring the controller up
verdicts.BLOCKED_FIRMWARE: a controller/module path exists but no NFC firmware blob is present
verdicts.BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_RESOURCE: kernel NFC is up but no userspace stack (neard/nfc-list) can talk to it
verdicts.NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_DEVICE: the shipped kernel/driver set provides no supported path at all for this controller
verdicts.PARTIAL: some stages present, some missing — read the per-stage lines
verdicts.BLOCKED_FIRMWARE_HASH: firmware file exists but its size/SHA-256 does not match the verified manifest entry
verdicts.SERVICE_STOPPED: hardware and firmware are present but nuxel-nfcd is not running; NFC is OFF

tag_test.comment: Owner procedure only. The repository never fabricates a tag UID; it scripts the read and asks the owner to compare the UID printed on the tag.
steps: have any NFC tag (NTAG213/215/216 or a MIFARE Classic card) on hand
start the reader (nfc-list / neard) as instructed by the diagnostic
place the tag flat on the phone's upper-back area for ~2 seconds
read the UID and compare it with the UID printed/known for that tag
record the UID, the tool used and the outcome in this fragment
evidence_required_for_promotion: nuxel-nfc-diag.sh status prints controller + firmware stages as present
the reader reports one tag with a UID matching the physical tag
a second read of a different tag yields a different UID
